Narrative: Across 34 cases from 1996 to 2026, the highest-value exits did the same six things in roughly the same order; Punctual Pros is about 30 months into its own version. First, the sponsor put an operator team in charge at entry: Alpine named Apex's CEO and CFO on launch day in July 2019 with $100M+ of committed equity, American Capital gave Service Experts' returning CEO about 10% ownership, and Huron recruited Sciens' CEO before it bought its first company. Second, the first add-on came early and close to home, a median of about 7 months after entry across 11 dated cases, as Smith + Howard did with Market Street Partners in month 9 and Punctual Pros did with Horvath in month 8. Third, the tuck-ins kept coming at roughly one every three to five months: Trivest did 16 at TurnPoint while revenue grew nearly 10x, Huron did 13 at Sciens while revenue and EBITDA rose more than 35x, and BSP did nine at Smith + Howard while headcount went from about 100 to about 800. Fourth, every brand ran on one system: CenterOak ran a single IT system and consolidated purchasing at Service Champions, Wrench now books online at 99% of its locations on ServiceTitan, and Authority Brands moved Punctual Pros and every other One Hour, Benjamin Franklin and Mister Sparky location onto ServiceTitan in September 2024. Fifth, they built recurring revenue that buyers pay for: Champions grew from about 60,000 members in 2021 to about 150,000 in 2026 (about 71 to 83 per technician) and sold to Blackstone in February 2026 at a reported ~18.5x trailing EBITDA, while Frontdoor gets 76% of its revenue from renewals with 84% of customers on auto-pay. Sixth, they owned the technician pipeline: Champions more than doubled its field technicians from 850 to 1,800+, Shermco grew certified technicians from 400+ to 600+ as Gryphon doubled revenue and sold for about $1.6B, and Sila bought a trade school in January 2026. Margin beat volume in the best compounders, as VWR grew Adjusted EBITDA 8.6% a year against 3.7% sales growth from 2006 to 2013 and IES grew operating income 88% on 21% more revenue in FY2024. In the last 12-18 months before a sale the winners kept buying and published KPIs: Shermco closed five add-ons in the 17 months before Blackstone, Sila added four brands in the nine months before Goldman's ~$1.7B (~17x) purchase, and Smith + Howard disclosed more than 600 employees and ~$175M of expected revenue about five months before TPG signed. Most exits went to a larger sponsor, often with the seller or management rolling equity (Charlesbank into GI Partners at ARS, Odyssey alongside Blackstone at Champions, BV alongside BSP at Frontline), and the median first-sponsor hold was about 4.4 years (4.0 in residential home services). The failures show what not to copy: Any Hour signed 16 partnerships in about 13 months and its loan now carries PIK at ~89% of par, TurnPoint grew from 17 to 65 brands and now pays PIK under a new CEO, Horizon is lender-supported, and Roto-Rooter's parent Chemed raised ad spend about $11M from 2023 to 2025 while segment revenue fell about $50M. For Punctual Pros the order is an integration leader and a ServiceTitan KPI pack now, members per technician as the north-star metric, one contiguous tuck-in per quarter in PA, NJ, MD and DE, a Lancaster academy with Thaddeus Stevens, leverage near the 2.9-3.3x lower-middle-market norm, and an exit-ready KPI pack by about 2028.

text:
Kind: use_case
Company: pp
Name: After-hours emergency dispatcher (One Hour / Ben Franklin / Mister Sparky / Horvath lines)
Direction: inbound
Trigger: Any call outside staffed hours (weekday 5pm-8am, weekends, holidays) to a brand tracking number.
Flow:
- Greets with the brand name and says it is the virtual assistant.
- Runs a safety screen first (gas smell, CO alarm, sparking, water near panel) and gives 911/utility instructions when triggered.
- Matches caller ID to the ServiceTitan customer and confirms address and equipment on file.
- Classifies the job (no heat, no cool, active leak, no power) and priority (infant/elderly, freezing temps, NWS warning active).
- Checks on-call technician capacity and offers the earliest arrival window.
- States that an after-hours diagnostic fee applies and texts the amount and terms.
- Books the job on the dispatch board, pages the on-call tech, and texts the customer a confirmation and on-my-way link.
- Writes transcript, summary and disposition to the job record.
Handoff rule: Transfer to the on-call manager when there is a safety hazard the caller cannot leave, a commercial account, a complaint or billing dispute, the caller asks for a person twice, or two failed intent attempts; target live pickup within 60s, otherwise callback promise within 10 minutes.
Kpis:
after-hours answer rate; after-hours booking rate; time to book (s); abandon rate during greeting; jobs booked per on-call shift; escalation rate
Est annual value ($): 390,000
Value label: assumption
Value formula: 42,024 calls/yr x 0.12 after-hours x 0.35 lost x 0.8 recovered x 0.45 booked x 0.6 incremental x $1,024 = $390,000
Weeks to deploy: 3
Risk notes: Over-promising arrival times when on-call capacity is thin; must never diagnose safety issues; the quoted fee must match the franchise price book; brand guarantee wording (One Hour on-time promise) only where the window is honored.
Source url: https://www.servicetitan.com/features/pro/voice-agent
Retrieved: 2026-10-06
Retrieval status: fetched
title: Voice AI research: After-hours emergency dispatcher (One Hour / Ben Franklin / Mister Sparky / Horvath lines)

abandon rate; storm-day booked jobs; share of overflow booked; average speed of answer; CSR occupancy

Risk notes: Surge can exceed field capacity, so the agent must stop offering same-day slots when the board is full and offer a waitlist; storm messaging must not promise insurance outcomes.

Text: Thanks for calling Benjamin Franklin Plumbing. Our team is helping other customers during today's storm, so I'm the virtual assistant and I can book you right now. Calls are reviewed for coaching. What's going on?
- Speaker: Caller
Text: Water's coming into my basement. I think the sump pump died.
- Speaker: Agent
Text: Let's get that handled. Is the water near any outlets, the electrical panel or appliances?
- Speaker: Caller
Text: It's about an inch deep. Not near the panel.
- Speaker: Agent
Text: Good. Please stay out of standing water near anything electrical. What's the address?
- Speaker: Caller
Text: 88 Ridge Road, Mount Joy.
- Speaker: Agent
Text: That's in our service area. Is the pump running without pumping, or completely silent?
- Speaker: Caller
Text: Silent. I already checked the outlet and the breaker.
- Speaker: Agent
Text: Thanks, that helps. With the flash flood warning we're putting active water first. The earliest window is 1 to 2 p.m. today, and the plumber will carry a replacement pump. Does that work?
- Speaker: Caller
Text: Yes. Can they look at my water heater too? It's down there.
- Speaker: Agent
Text: I've added a water-heater safety check to the job notes. Can I text the confirmation to the mobile number ending in 4417?
- Speaker: Caller
Text: Yes, that's my cell.
- Speaker: Agent
Text: You're booked for 1 to 2 p.m. today. You'll get a text when your plumber is on the way, along with our on-time guarantee details. If the water reaches the panel, leave the basement and call your utility.
- Speaker: Caller
Text: Thank you, really.
Outcome: Active-water job booked same day ahead of non-urgent calls under the storm triage rule; add-on inspection noted; CSRs stayed on the phones they were already handling.

text:
Kind: architecture
Layer: pipeline
Name: Reference 24/7 dispatch call pipeline (cascaded)
Pipeline:
- Hop: telephony
What: Brand tracking number -> Twilio/SIP; brand greeting that names the virtual assistant; caller ID passed to the agent.
Budget ms: network/PSTN ~230 (mouth-to-ear 1,115 minus platform 885)
- Hop: streaming ASR + end-of-turn
What: Deepgram/AssemblyAI streaming with brand and township keyword boosting; semantic end-of-turn detection.
Budget ms: 350
Upper ms: 500
- Hop: LLM with tools
What: Claude (Messages API, streaming, strict tool schemas) decides the next utterance or tool call.
Budget ms: 375
Upper ms: 750
Tools:
customer_lookup(phone|address) -> ServiceTitan customer/location/equipment; check_capacity(zip, job_type, priority) -> open windows (Adaptive Capacity); book_job(customer_id, job_type, window, notes) -> job_id; send_payment_link(customer_id, amount_type) -> SMS link (no card data in voice); page_on_call(trade, priority, summary) -> acknowledgement; transfer_to_human(queue, summary) -> warm transfer; log_disposition(call_id, outcome, contact_preferences)
- Hop: TTS
What: Brand voice per franchise (ElevenLabs Flash or Cartesia Sonic), streamed sentence by sentence.
Budget ms: 100
Upper ms: 250
Latency budget:
Platform turn gap target ms: 885
Platform upper ms: 1100
Mouth to ear target ms: 1115
Mouth to ear upper ms: 1400
Human benchmark ms: 200
Tool call rule: Tool calls that exceed ~700 ms get a spoken filler ('Let me check the schedule...') so the turn gap never exceeds the 1.4 s upper limit.
Human handoff: Warm transfer with a spoken + written summary to the CSR queue (business hours) or on-call manager (after hours) on: safety hazard, explicit request for a person (second ask), two failed intents, payment dispute, VIP/commercial account, low ASR confidence on address after two tries. If no human answers within 60 s, the agent books a guaranteed callback and pages the manager.
Logging qa: Every call: recording, transcript, tool-call log, model/prompt version, disposition and greeting check. Score 100% of transcripts with an LLM rubric (safety screen asked, virtual-assistant introduction given, booking asked, correct fee wording) and have a human review a weighted 5% sample plus every escalation and complaint weekly.
Est cost per minute ($): 0.1158
Est cost breakdown per minute:
Telephony inbound: 0.0085
Recording: 0.0025
Asr deepgram nova3: 0.0048
Llm estimate: 0.03
Tts estimate: 0.02
Orchestration vapi: 0.05
Est cost note: Cascaded build ~$0.1158/min (LLM and TTS are estimates); a 4-minute call costs ~$0.46, vs $1.67-$3.00 per call for Smith.ai and $0.12-0.14/min all-in on Bland.
Source url: https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/developers/best-practices/guide-core-latency-ai-voice-agents
Retrieved: 2026-10-06
Retrieval status: fetched
title: Voice AI research: Reference 24/7 dispatch call pipeline (cascaded)

text:
Missed-call economics, vendors, use cases and guardrails

Generated: 2026-10-06
Portfolio company focus: pp
Method: Web research on 2026-10-06 (WebSearch/WebFetch) of vendor pricing pages, benchmark reports, case studies and funding coverage; figures were taken from the fetched page where possible (retrieval status 'fetched'), otherwise from the search-engine result for the cited URL ('search snippet'), or reused from sourced items already in this repo ('portal data': pp_ads.json, pp_nationwide.json, ai_agents_portfolio.json). The Punctual Pros revenue model is computed in code from pp_demand_model.json call baselines, pp_nationwide.json core housing units and the cited benchmarks; every use-case value is a labelled assumption with its formula.
Caveats:
- Vendor outcome numbers (booking rates, CSAT, deflection, ROI) are self-reported and unaudited; use them as ranges, not promises.
- Punctual Pros' actual call volume, missed-call rate, booking rate, membership count and tickets are not public; the model backs call volume out of the ~$22M revenue estimate and must be recalibrated from ServiceTitan data.
- Market call baselines (Punctual Pros demand model) are derived from homeowner surveys and are themselves estimates.
- Several benchmark pages were gated or not fetchable (Invoca report body, Azure pricing, PubMed HTML); items say so via retrieval status.
- Healthcare no-show evidence (Parikh 2010) is a proxy for home-service confirmations.
- Sample calls are illustrative scripts with fictional customers, addresses and technicians.
Thesis:
- Every unanswered call to a home-services company is a buyer with an urgent problem who will call the next number on Google, so phone coverage is a revenue line.
- Invoca's 2026 benchmark finds only 52% of home-services callers reach a person (65% of real calls over 15 seconds), and 55% of businesses never ask the caller to book.
- The leaks cluster exactly when demand peaks: ServiceTitan data show off-hours calls rise to 14% of HVAC inbound in June, and trades lose 30-40% of them.
- Speed decides who wins the job, because a lead called within 5 minutes is 21 times more likely to qualify than one called at 30 minutes (MIT/InsideSales), and the odds keep falling by the hour (HBR).
- AI voice agents now book at human-or-better rates: ServiceTitan reports 70% overall and 90% when capacity is open, versus a 42% typical human CSR booking rate.
- For Punctual Pros, a conservative model (about 3,502 inbound calls a month, 15% missed, 45% booked, 40% haircut for callers who would have called back) recovers about $1.4M a year of jobs from calls that go unanswered today.
- Outbound AI turns the member list into scheduled revenue, and an 8-point renewal lift on an assumed 6,000 members adds about $403k a year before tune-up upsell.
- At roughly $0.12 a minute for a self-built stack (or $1.67-$3 a call bought off the shelf), the cost is a rounding error against a $1,024 average repair ticket.
- The same engine runs for every portfolio company: emergency lines for CET, a password-reset desk for Frontline, reorder lines for Thomas Scientific, a press line for BPI and order help for Fair Harbor.
- Built with a clear virtual-assistant greeting, human handoff and 100% transcript QA, 24/7 voice coverage becomes a measurable, data-room-ready growth engine that raises booked revenue without adding headcount.
Pp revenue model:
Inbound calls per month: 3502
Inbound calls formula: market calls/month = (HVAC 10 + plumbing 16 + electrical 7) calls/day per 10k households (Punctual Pros demand model baselines) x 1,001,408 core housing units / 10,000 x 30.42 days = 100,516; PP share is not public, so it is backed out of revenue: PP call-driven jobs = $22M x 70% / $1,024 = 15,039/yr; inbound calls = jobs / (answer rate 0.852 x human booking rate 0.42) = 42,027/yr = 3,502/month => implied PP share of market reactive calls = 3.5%.
Market calls per month core: 100,516
Implied pp share of market calls: 0.0348
Missed share: 0.148
Missed share formula: after-hours share 0.12 x after-hours lost 0.35 + daytime share 0.88 x daytime missed/abandoned 0.12 = 0.148
Missed share range:
0.1; 0.35
Recovered share with ai: 0.8
Booking rate: 0.45
Incrementality: 0.6
Avg ticket: 1024
Recovered revenue annual ($): 1,372,000
Recovered revenue formula: 3,502 calls/mo x 12 x missed 0.148 x recovered 0.8 x booking 0.45 x incrementality 0.6 x $1,024 = 1,343 incremental jobs x $1,024 = $1,372,000 (after-hours $390,000 + daytime/storm overflow $982,000)
Outbound renewal uplift ($): 403,000
Outbound renewal formula: 6,000 members x (0.88 - 0.8) renewal lift x (fee $240 + member service revenue $600) = $403,000
Total est ($): 1,775,000
Share of pp revenue: 0.081
Sensitivity:
Missed share 0.35 invoca industry: 3,253,000
Booking 0.70 servicetitan ai: 2,140,000
Incrementality 1.0: 2,293,000
Members 3000: 202,000
Assumptions:
- Market baselines: Punctual Pros demand model HVAC 10, plumbing 16, electrical 7 reactive calls/day per 10k households (market-wide, all providers), applied to 1,001,408 core housing units (Punctual Pros nationwide plan and ZIP coverage).
- PP revenue ~$22M (repo estimate); 70% of it assumed to start with an inbound call (rest: replacements sold on site, memberships, commercial).
- Average ticket $1,024 = Housecall Pro 2025 HVAC repair revenue per job $1,205 x 0.85 to reflect lower plumbing/electrical repair tickets (assumption); LSA-sourced tickets ($1,434-$2,110) include replacements and are not used.
- Missed share 0.148: after-hours calls are ~12% of HVAC inbound (ServiceTitan 2025: 9.8% Oct to 14.1% Jun) and trades lose 30-40% of them (ServiceTitan webinar); daytime missed/abandoned 12% is an assumption for a staffed CSR team, well below Invoca's 35% industry rate for calls >15s.
- Recovered share 0.8: the AI answers every call on the first ring but some callers hang up on hearing an assistant or are not service leads (spam, vendors, wrong numbers).
- Booking rate 0.45: Invoca's 45% lead-conversion-on-call, deliberately below ServiceTitan's 70% (90% capacity-adjusted) AI booking rate because recovered calls include non-bookable calls.
- Incrementality 0.6: 40% of recovered callers are assumed to have called back or booked anyway; ServiceTitan customers describe AI-booked overflow jobs as incremental, so this is conservative.
- Renewals: 6,000 active members (assumption; replace with ServiceTitan membership count), base renewal 80% (Applause HQ), AI outbound lifts it to 88% (assumption informed by vendor-reported automated vs manual lapse rates), fee $20/month (Applause $15-30 range), $600 extra service revenue per member-year (assumption; Sera reports members spend ~2.5x non-members).
- Not counted: speed-to-lead callbacks, unsold-estimate follow-up, no-show reduction and the Spanish line (valued separately in use case items), CSR labor savings, and storm-day surge pricing.
- Calibrate every input in month 1 from ServiceTitan call-tracking (missed/abandoned by hour), booking-rate reports and membership exports; replace assumptions before quoting externally.

Purpose: Feed for an on-page 'revenue at risk' ticker (debt-clock style). Uses the same conservative inputs as Punctual Pros revenue model; it is the revenue the 24/7 AI layer is modelled to recover, i.e. what is estimated to leak today from unanswered calls.

Read the program summary

45 AI agents cover BSP's six active companies, one set per operating system (ServiceOS, GridOS, FirmOS, LabOS, SignalOS, HarborOS), built from 8 reusable patterns. Each agent starts on an event, such as a missed call, an NWS alert, a deed record, a bid posting or an invoice, so no one has to remember to start it. Every agent also names the person who approves its consequential actions; no agent moves money, prices below a margin floor, posts publicly or disables an account on its own.
On labelled analyst assumptions the program is worth about $12.7M a year of run-rate EBITDA-equivalent value once ramped, led by Thomas Scientific ($3.8M) and Frontline ($3.6M). Punctual Pros ($0.9M) gets the most agents per dollar of revenue because missed calls, dispatch, options, memberships and permits are where home-services margin is won or lost. CET ($1.3M) uses agents to pick better bids, estimate faster and turn NuWave and EV monitoring into recurring revenue.
BPI ($2.3M) and Fair Harbor ($0.8M) use agents to productize monitoring, protect client confidentiality while drafting faster, and cut returns and excess inventory. Rollout runs in four waves over 18 months, starting with inbound-contact and document agents that have the clearest baselines and lowest risk, then finance, then revenue agents, then monitoring services. PRG governance sets least-privilege access, consequence-based approval tiers, full audit logs, approved model terms with no training on portfolio data, vendor AI reviews, and kill criteria tied to measured value.
Values are estimates built from vendor case studies and public benchmarks with explicit haircuts; each must be re-based on the company's own 8-week baseline before it is counted in an exit narrative like Smith + Howard's.
Overlay on this page: the $12.7M is a ceiling. Net of estimated run costs and risk-adjusted by value type it is $3.3M–$5.3M a year; see Program economics. Thomas Scientific's inventory agent moves to wave 2, and the wave-1 gate adds the legal-confidentiality control for Frontline.

Build cost = weeks to go live × engineer share (buy 0.25, hybrid 0.5, build 1) × $5,000/week (a ~$250K loaded agent engineer) + $20K for implementation, an evaluation set and a 30-day pilot.
Run cost a year = vendor licence (buy $36K, hybrid $30K, build $0) + model and hosting spend (buy $0, hybrid $12K, build $24K) + $25K upkeep (0.1 engineer). The licence is skipped for the 7 formulas that already subtract a software or unit cost.
Engineers per wave = engineer-weeks ÷ weeks in the wave, rounded up. The plan's wave-1 gate named one engineer; six agents in 13 weeks need about 17 engineer-weeks, so 2.
Payback = build cost ÷ monthly risk-adjusted value net of run cost (mid case: capacity counted at 25%).

Caveats on the figures

All estimated annual value figures are assumptions, not company data; volumes (calls, tickets, invoices, quotes, members) are analyst estimates and must be replaced with system-of-record counts.
Most metric claim figures come from vendor case studies (Avoca, ServiceTitan, Rilla, Togal.AI, Vic.ai, Conexiom, HighRadius, Proton.ai, Gorgias, Loopio, Rewst, Intapp); they are self-selected and unaudited, so values apply roughly 50% haircuts.

About a third of the ceiling is freed capacity valued at loaded rates; it becomes EBITDA only with a hiring-avoidance or headcount plan.

Decision rules
When to buy, build or mix

Buy when the agent lives inside the system of record. If ServiceTitan, Procore or Gorgias ships it natively, speed beats differentiation; a buyer will not pay more for a home-built dispatch board.

Build when the agent's memory is BSP data. Bid go or no-go on CET's bid radar, weather surge on Punctual Pros' storm history, grant signals from NIH RePORTER, docket tracking: that scoring is the IP that makes an OS an OS at exit.

Hybrid by default for documents. Buy extraction or transport (Conexiom, Vic.ai, Intapp), build the exception queue, disclosure and audit layer once and reuse it across companies.

Every purchase passes the vendor AI review (control 5). A 30-day pilot against the company's own baseline, SOC 2 Type II, no training on portfolio data, and an exit and export clause.

Never single-source the model. Route small models to extraction and frontier models to drafting; keep a second provider qualified for failover (control 4).

Design and program rationale
An operating partner approves a wave in one meeting

One system, not a feature dump
Give every agent the same anatomy: trigger, agent, approver. Forty-five then scan as one system.
KPI: time to approve a wave; agents stopped vs shipped per quarter.

Controls up front
Show the controls, owners and evidence before anyone asks for them.
KPI: diligence questions answered from the page; tier-3 incidents (target 0).

Lead with the number
One headline figure, with its cost and risk-adjusted net beside it. Every figure stays an estimate until measured.
KPI: share of the $12.7M ceiling re-based on measured baselines; capacity value counted only with a hiring plan.

Institutional tone, sources on every claim
Sober type and a source on every claim. It should read as a memo, not a pitch.
KPI: agents backed by a measured result at a comparable company: 16 of 45 today (10 more cite a benchmark, 19 only context); target 45 of 45 via pilots.

Sources and method
Terms, sources, assumptions

Terms. ERP: the accounting and order system. CRM: the customer and sales system. O&M: operations and maintenance. DSO: days customers take to pay. RFQ: request for quote.

Sources. Portfolio AI-agent plan and tech-enablement evidence (generated Oct 2026), including OS EBITDA cases and adjusted EBITDA estimates, vendor or build path per agent; costs, haircuts and ramp are analyst overlays on this page. All figures are estimates; values are ceilings, and each agent cites its evidence.

Ceiling. A year once every agent is ramped, before run costs, not de-duplicated. Risk-adjusted by value type and net of estimated run costs. Costs are assumptions until quoted.

Hard cost-out: counted at 100%.
Working-capital carry: counted at 100% (interest on cash released).
Margin on revenue lift & leakage recovery: counted at 50% (overlaps between agents, unproven at our scale).
New recurring products: counted at 50% (needs buyers and contracts).
Freed capacity (hours × loaded rate): counted at 0–50%: EBITDA only with a hiring-avoidance or headcount plan.

11 agents ($4.0M, 31% of the ceiling) are hours saved × loaded rate. That is EBITDA only if a company hires fewer people or redeploys them to billable work, so each one needs a named hiring-avoidance plan before it is counted. Only 7 of 45 value formulas subtract a run cost; the run costs here are charged to the other 38.

The ask. Budget covers engineering, implementation, eval sets and pilots; figures are estimates until vendor quotes arrive. Controls 1–5 live everywhere before go-live; control 6 and the confidentiality evidence pack before the Frontline service desk touches law-firm data. Full ceiling run-rate arrives around Q2-28 (month 21), not month 18: agents ramp over two quarters after go-live.

Rollout calendar. Red line: Thomas Scientific loan maturity, December 2027. Calendar assumes approval this month (month 0 = Oct 2026). Live at wave end assumes each agent goes live its stated number of weeks after the wave starts and ramps evenly to full value over two quarters, the same window the kill rule uses. The full $12.7M ceiling run-rate arrives around Q2-28, not month 18.

Wave 1 gate. Controls 1–5 live at every company (access, approval tiers, audit log, model terms and vendor review), because three wave-1 agents talk to customers; control 6 and its confidentiality evidence pack live before the Frontline service desk touches law-firm data; 8-week KPI baselines captured; 2 agent engineers (about 17 engineer-weeks in 13 weeks) and a named owner in each company.
Wave 2 gate. Wave-1 agents meeting at least 50% of target; shared document-triage and exception-queue service in production; payments firewall (control 7) signed off by each CFO.
Wave 3 gate. Clean master data in each system of record (ServiceTitan pricebook/memberships, Procore commitments, ERP SKUs/CAS map, Klaviyo profiles); customer contact lists cleaned.
Wave 4 gate. Monitoring agents priced as recurring services (contracts, SLAs, client reporting); AI-content labeling live at BPI and Fair Harbor. (The Frontline confidentiality evidence pack moved to the wave-1 gate.)

Risks

What could go wrong, and the hedge.

High
Field adoption
Foremen reject another app; dashboards go stale.
Hedge: mobile-first, one foreman champion per office, daily logs tied to bonuses.

High
Operational-technology security
Remote SCADA access widens the attack surface of a water system.
Hedge: segmented networks, multi-factor sign-in, no inbound ports, CISA water-sector alignment, owner sign-off.

Medium
Three companies, three systems
CET, Horton and NuWave run different job-cost and payroll stacks.
Hedge: build the data layer first; defer ERP consolidation past year one.

Medium
Slow municipal contracting
Assure and SCADA monitoring contracts move at council speed.
Hedge: offer monitoring as a priced O&M option at SRF project close-out.

Medium
Over-claiming the multiple
Re-rating is the least certain lever; the spread is only about 3 turns.
Hedge: underwrite on EBITDA; 0.5–1.5 turns is upside.

Low
Vendor lock-in and pricing
Volume pricing grows with backlog; long contracts limit switching.
Hedge: own the data layer; negotiate multi-company terms as add-ons join.

Targets and method
Latency limits, cost basis, sources

Reference 24/7 dispatch call pipeline (cascaded). Targets follow Twilio's latency guide: a 885 ms platform turn gap (upper limit 1,100 ms) and 1,115 ms mouth to ear (upper limit 1,400 ms). People leave about 200 ms between turns.
Tool calls that exceed ~700 ms get a spoken filler ('Let me check the schedule...') so the turn gap never exceeds the 1.4 s upper limit.
Cascaded build ~$0.1158/min (LLM and TTS are estimates); a 4-minute call costs ~$0.46, vs $1.67-$3.00 per call for Smith.ai and $0.12-0.14/min all-in on Bland. Twilio latency guide. Costs are per minute; model and voice costs are estimates. Vendor pricing pages, Oct 2026.

Human handoff in full. Warm transfer with a spoken + written summary to the CSR queue (business hours) or on-call manager (after hours) on: safety hazard, explicit request for a person (second ask), two failed intents, payment dispute, VIP/commercial account, low ASR confidence on address after two tries. If no human answers within 60 s, the agent books a guaranteed callback and pages the manager.
Logging and QA. Every call: recording, transcript, tool-call log, model/prompt version, disposition and greeting check. Score 100% of transcripts with an LLM rubric (safety screen asked, virtual-assistant introduction given, booking asked, correct fee wording) and have a human review a weighted 5% sample plus every escalation and complaint weekly.

Telephony Twilio Programmable Voice + ConversationRelay twilio.com Twilio's Nov 2025 benchmark: 1,115 ms median mouth-to-ear turn gap (1,400 upper), 885 ms platform turn gap (1,100 upper). $1.15/number/month; $0.0085/min inbound; $0.014/min outbound; $0.0025/min recording; ConversationRelay $0.07/min. Rules in full
Escalation, logging, scoring, change control

Escalation and human-handoff SLAs. Safety hazard → warm transfer to on-call within 60 s (else 911/utility instruction + page); explicit second request for a human → transfer within 60 s business hours, callback within 10 min after hours; complaint/billing dispute → human same day; weekly review of every escalation; target escalation rate 10-20% in month 1, falling with tuning.
Vendors build live escalation into AI CSRs (ServiceTitan: live escalation to human agents; Cresta at Brinks Home cut transfers from 30% to 8% while raising FCR to 92%). The aim is fewer transfers that land faster, not zero transfers.
Source: servicetitan.com · page read Oct 2026
QA sampling, logging and model change control. Score 100% of calls automatically against a rubric (greeting, safety screen, booking asked, fee wording, tone); humans review a 5% weighted sample plus all escalations and complaints; re-run a fixed test-call suite before any prompt/model/voice change; treat a wrong safety instruction or unauthorized price as a P1 incident with a 48-hour root-cause note.
NIST AI 600-1 (Generative AI Profile, July 2024) recommends documented pre-launch testing, ongoing monitoring and incident response for generative AI; the portfolio AI-agent plan (control 3) sets 3-7 year log retention by company.
Source: nvlpubs.nist.gov · portfolio data

08 · Risks

What breaks the plan, and what we do about it.

High
Election-cycle cyclicality
Gross federal political billings went from about $3.1M in 2022 to $115.3M in 2024, a fee swing of roughly $6–17M (est.).
Mitigation. SignalOS retainers plus corporate and international mix: 55% recurring revenue and at least 95% of net revenue kept in the post-election year (lever 3).

High
Political-client concentration
99% of 2024-cycle federal political billings came from one campaign committee, roughly $6–17M of fee revenue (est.). A buyer will test this first.
Mitigation. Grow the corporate and international retainer mix (levers 1 and 3), and add top-20 client concentration to the 30-day data request (ask 2) so the exit story is told on actuals.

High
AI substitutes for agency work
The Writer-commissioned Forrester TEI reports clients cutting external agency scope by 50%. 79% of PR firms already use AI for writing.
Mitigation. Own the AI layer instead of competing with it: price on outcomes (agent 8), compliance-gated drafting, the AI-fluency academy.

High
Senior talent and founders leave
Revenue follows the senior bench (LaBolt, Gibbs, Alexander, Whiting) and the founders of acquired firms. FGS, Teneo and Brunswick recruit from the same pool.
Mitigation. Partner equity pool on the FGS model, founder-to-practice-leader paths, earn-outs that outlast integration.

Med
Integrating six add-ons across six countries
Six add-ons in about three years, across six countries, three brands and multiple P&Ls. Germany now holds two acquired teams (BOLDT, Dec 2023, and 365 Sherpas, May 2026).
Mitigation. 100-day integration office, one knowledge base (agent 7), shared delivery and finance systems before the next add-on closes.

Med
Baseline estimates could be wrong
Net revenue of $85–125M and EBITDA of $17–28M are low-confidence estimates from headcount, the Form D and FEC filings.
Mitigation. First PRG ask: within 30 days, re-anchor the roadmap on actuals (mix by office, retainer share, comp ratio).

Med
Federal eligibility and incumbents
Tracked recompetes total about $250M, dominated by the NASA ceiling. Set-aside status is unverified and BPI has no prime past performance.
Mitigation. Capture team with teaming agreements (prime-sub) first; buy a contractor with schedule vehicles only if the pipeline justifies it.

Med
Competition for add-ons
8 sponsors overlap BPI in the private-equity landscape, MidOcean and CIVC rated high threat. Shamrock now owns Penta.
Mitigation. Proprietary sourcing through the Index briefings and Mandala, and pre-agreed DDTL capacity so BPI can close fast.

Med
FX and European exposure
International share rises from ~17% to 30% (est.). The UK estimate assumes GBP/USD of 1.27.
Mitigation. Local cost base as a natural hedge, and a multi-currency DDTL tranche.

A memo, not a brochure

Sources and caveats
Estimate basis, vendor limits, filings

BPI revenue, EBITDA, headcount and debt are low-confidence analyst estimates from BPI public filings, not company disclosures. Every KPI target and roadmap figure is an assumption, labelled est.
FEC figures are gross political billings, mostly pass-through media, not BPI revenue.
Penta revenue ($100M+, about half from AI and data) is as reported by Axios (Aug 2025); other coverage confirms the deal but not the revenue.
The Teneo valuation (~$700M) comes from press summaries. The CVC release confirms 800+ staff, 19 offices and 9 acquisitions since 2015, but not the price.
AI-agent metrics come from vendor-commissioned studies or vendor case studies and are self-selected upper bounds. The Writer study also shows clients cutting agency scope by 50%, a substitution risk for BPI.
The $250M federal opportunity total sums contract ceilings and is dominated by the NASA recompete ($202.6M with all options). Eligibility and set-aside status are unverified.
No ask assumes new equity; add-ons run on the existing senior facility. Risks are ranked by how badly each would hurt the exit: the biggest is the election cycle, the newest is AI replacing agency work.
International revenue share (~15–20% today) is an analyst estimate from UK Companies House staff counts at an assumed GBP/USD of 1.27. Germany and Nordics revenue is not public.
Sources: BPI public filings (Form D, FEC, Companies House), the BSP firm profile, public comparables, the private-equity landscape, OS program evidence and competitor filings (FGS, Precision Strategies, Stagwell), plus public releases and research read in October 2026. Method: phase data points are computed from those sources (add-on cadences, ratios, sums of contract ceilings); KPI targets and the 36-month roadmap are analyst assumptions anchored to the midpoints of the public-filings estimates.

FAQ

Questions clients ask first.

What does BPI do?
A strategic communications and public affairs firm. Six practices work as one team: public affairs, corporate reputation, campaigns, research, digital and paid media, and AI communications.

Which offices do you have?
Washington, DC (headquarters), New York, Chicago, San Francisco, Los Angeles and Boston in the US; London, Brussels, Berlin, Oslo and Zurich/Geneva in Europe; and Asia-Pacific coverage through the Mandala Partners alliance in Australia.

What is SignalOS?
SignalOS is the proposed intelligence layer under every BPI retainer: always-on narrative monitoring, synthetic-audience message testing validated with live panels, a compliance-gated content studio and outcome dashboards. It turns monitoring and measurement into a subscription rather than a line item.

How do retainers and pricing work?
Most work runs on monthly retainers; campaigns and research are scoped as projects. The concept adds three tiers (Monitor, Advise, Command) with illustrative prices.

How fast can you respond in a crisis?
Under the proposed SignalOS retainers, alerts arrive with a draft holding statement. The response target is 2 hours on Monitor and 30 minutes on Advise and Command.

Can you test our message before we launch it?
Yes. Message House, the elite-audience research group BPI acquired in Nov 2024, tests messages with policymakers, investors and other hard-to-reach audiences across EMEA. SignalOS adds synthetic pre-tests that narrow options in hours before live fieldwork confirms the finalists.

Do you work in Brussels and Berlin?
Yes. BOLDT (December 2023) and 365 Sherpas (May 2026) made Germany BPI’s third-largest market. One retainer can cover Washington, Brussels and Berlin.

What is AI communications?
AI policy positioning, deepfake and misinformation response, and AI-assisted content with review checkpoints. In BPI’s 2026 survey, 81% of adults said AI spreads false rumours too easily.

Do you work with sports organizations?
Yes. BPI formalized a sports offering in Oct 2024 and scaled it with the May 2025 acquisition of Agado Communications, whose founder Mark Jones leads BPI’s sports strategy and growth.

Do you handle litigation and regulatory risk?
Yes. In Mar 2026 BPI launched a litigation communications, oversight and regulatory-risk offering led by partner Elizabeth E. Alexander, covering congressional oversight, investigations and enforcement actions.

Who leads BPI?
Andrew Bleeker is CEO and Ben LaBolt has been President since Apr 2025. BSP made a majority investment in Apr 2023; Svoboda Capital Partners remains an investor.

Are you hiring?
The concept careers section lists illustrative openings across public affairs, research, SignalOS data engineering and corporate affairs in Washington, New York, London, Berlin and Chicago.

What this is

This memo reviews BSP's six portfolio companies using public records only. It shows where each company stands, where profit can grow fastest and what to do in the first 90 days. Figures not found in public filings are analyst estimates, marked est., to be checked against company actuals.

Terms: EBITDA is operating profit before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization. EV is enterprise value. A “turn” is one times EBITDA added to the sale price. DSO (days sales outstanding) is how long customers take to pay. Each OS (operating system) is a bundle of software and AI tools for one company. PP is Punctual Pros.

09 · Questions

Answers, before you call.

What does Thomas Scientific sell?
Six categories for working labs: consumables, equipment, chemicals, safety & PPE, cleanroom and cold chain, plus services that keep them stocked (vendor-managed inventory, punchout, kitting).

Do you supply cleanroom consumables and garments?
Yes. ISO Class 5–8 wipes, sterile garments and coveralls, sterile IPA, tacky mats and gowning-room supplies. Our Northeast cleanroom specialists joined from Quintana Supply (Haverhill, MA) and Day Associates (Dracut, MA), both acquired in 2023.

Do you serve cannabis and hemp testing labs?
Yes. HPLC and LC-MS-grade solvents, amber autosampler vials, syringe filters, balances, PPE and audit-ready CoA/SDS documentation, shipped together so potency and residual-solvent testing never waits on one missing line.

How does pricing work? Can I get a quote?
Accounts get contract pricing by volume and category. Build a quote cart from any product (or paste catalog numbers into Quick Order) and a specialist returns pricing. Concept target: same business day.

How do I set up a punchout catalog?
We connect to the procurement system you already use (Coupa, SAP Ariba, Jaggaer and other cXML/OCI systems). Buyers shop at your contract prices and the cart returns as a requisition.

What is vendor-managed inventory (VMI)?
We own the min/max for the stockrooms you choose: scan-based or scheduled counts, automatic replenishment, consignment for critical items and a monthly usage review. Your scientists stop placing reorders.

Can you build custom kits?
Yes. Specimen-collection kits, evidence-collection kits, new-hire and gowning kits, and protocol-specific packs assembled under one catalog number. Forensics kitting builds on Arrowhead Forensics (Lenexa, KS).

Who is my account representative?
Pick your state in the Find your lab team section. It shows your regional team, the hub that serves you and how many lab sites we already map in your state.

Do you ship temperature-sensitive products?
Yes. ULT freezers and lab refrigerators, dry-ice and insulated shippers, and USB temperature loggers with PDF reports for chain-of-custody records.

Where can I find CoA and SDS documents?
Certificates of Analysis and Safety Data Sheets attach to every product and order line in the document center, searchable by catalog number or lot.

Where do you ship from?
Headquarters and distribution in Swedesboro, NJ, with regional teams from North Central Instruments (Brooklyn Park, MN), Quintana Supply and Day Associates (Massachusetts) and Arrowhead Forensics (Lenexa, KS).

How long has Thomas Scientific been in business?
Since 1900, more than 125 years of supplying laboratories. BSP became the majority investor in January 2022.

Are you hiring?
Distribution, customer service, inside sales and lab specialists. In production a careers page would list open roles by distribution center.

What is LabOS?
LabOS is the operating layer behind this site: AI product search, punchout and B2B commerce, vendor-managed inventory, supplier-consolidation analytics and account-health scoring. See the LabOS product page →

Closing the gap

2.1x and ~16% IRR is a weak base case for lower-middle-market PE.

08 · Eyes open

What could go wrong, and what we need from the PRG.

Risks and mitigations
The numbers are estimates, not disclosures
Revenue ($100-140M), EBITDA ($16-20M) and margin are leverage and headcount assumptions.Mitigation: Rebase the KPI roadmap on monthly management accounts within 30 days.
The entry multiple may not hold at exit
Entry at ~12-15x sits above MSP deal comps (9.9-11.2x by size); the exit multiple may compress.Mitigation: Hold recurring mix above 50%, churn below 10% and cyber attach; EBITDA growth carries the return.
The add-on plan outruns the debt
~$50-80M of add-on spend against ~$15-35M of incremental debt capacity.Mitigation: Plan a $20–45M co-invest top-up now, starting with the $7.5M unsold in the Frontline co-invest vehicle.
Client count and churn are unreconciled
Press releases say 800-900+ firms; the homepage says 300. Churn and recurring mix are not public.Mitigation: Reconcile both and disclose the revolver or delayed-draw facility before any sale process.
Consolidators bid up legal MSPs
Alpine (Evergreen), New Charter, CIVC and EagleTree all buy in IT or legal services.Mitigation: Move first on founder-owned targets (Tabush, Garver, Legal Billing Group); keep local brands, as Smith + Howard did.
AI results are vendor claims
Moveworks (25-35%), HighRadius and Laurel figures are vendor-published; HELIX has no published deflection metric.Mitigation: Run every pilot against a control group; publish deflection and DSO monthly.
International is a foothold, not a business
The UK subsidiary booked ~GBP 0.58M in 2024; SRA-regulated clients raise the bar.Mitigation: Buy, don't build: acquire Quiss or ALB; staff UK hours from Cape Town.

FAQ

Good questions. Straight answers.

What areas do you serve?
Nine Central Pennsylvania counties from our East Hempfield headquarters, plus Ocean and Monmouth counties on the Jersey Shore through Horvath Home Services. Check your ZIP in the coverage checker.

How does the on-time guarantee work?
You pick a two-hour window and we text a live ETA when the technician is on the way. If we arrive late, we pay you for the wait. (Terms are illustrative.)

How much does a service call cost?
We use upfront, flat-rate pricing. The technician diagnoses the problem, then shows good, better and best options with the full price before any work starts. Comfort Club members pay no diagnostic fee. (Prices on this concept site are illustrative.)

What is the Comfort Club membership?
A monthly plan with two HVAC tune-ups a year, repair discounts, no diagnostic or after-hours fees and priority scheduling. The savings calculator shows what it is worth to you.

Do you offer financing for a new system?
Yes. Replacements can be spread over 5 to 10 years, subject to credit approval through a lending partner. Try the payment estimator. We also file the utility rebates for you.

What rebates can I get for a heat pump or water heater?
In PA, PPL, FirstEnergy (Met-Ed) and UGI rebate heat pumps, furnaces and water heaters; in NJ, SAVEGREEN and JCP&L do. The federal 25C credit ended on December 31, 2025. See the live list.

Are you open nights, weekends and holidays?
Yes, 24/7/365 for no-heat, no-cool, leaks, backups and electrical hazards. After hours, our AI dispatcher can book a real slot and page the on-call technician immediately.

Which brands are you?
Punctual Pros operates One Hour Heating & Air Conditioning, Benjamin Franklin Plumbing and Mister Sparky franchises across 25 territories in Pennsylvania and New Jersey (2026 franchise disclosure documents). Horvath Home Services joined in December 2024.

Do you install generators, EV chargers and panel upgrades?
Yes. Mister Sparky handles panel upgrades, surge protection, Level 2 EV chargers and whole-home standby generators, including permits and utility coordination.

Are your technicians licensed and background-checked?
Every technician is licensed for their trade, background-checked and drug-tested, and trained on the same flat-rate pricebook. License numbers would be listed on every page (placeholders in this concept).

Are you hiring technicians?
Yes. A recent Punctual Pros HVAC Service Technician posting in Lancaster listed $70,000–$120,000 a year. We also hire apprentices and pay for training. See careers.

I own a home-services business. Would you acquire it?
We partner with respected HVAC, plumbing and electrical companies in PA, NJ, MD and DE. Horvath Home Services joined in 2024 and kept its name and team. Start a confidential conversation.

What is ServiceOS?
ServiceOS is the software behind every visit: weather-aware capacity planning, a live dispatch board, an AI dispatcher for after-hours calls, membership automation and new-mover outreach. See how it works.

How do you prepare for storms and cold snaps?
Our dispatchers watch live National Weather Service alerts and a seven-day Service-Call Pressure Index. Before a freeze or a storm we stage technicians, stock generator and sump parts, and hold same-day slots for members. Check the storm-readiness panel.

Design principles
Ten rules every concept follows

01
One primary action above the fold, attached to the input.
A headline, one field and one button: a ZIP code, an email or a chat prompt. Everything else is a ghost button or a link.
KPI: Hero click-through, questions asked per visit and booked jobs per session.

02
Show live, real numbers early; scale beats adjectives.
A stat band computed from real data (ZIP codes, opportunities, staff, locations) with units and a source line. Illustrative figures are always labelled.
KPI: Scroll depth past the stat band, time on page and credibility in user tests.

03
Show the product, not stock imagery.
Real interface screenshots in device frames, or a working demo such as a dispatch board, a bid board or trust controls. Each OS page leads with its interactive demo.
KPI: Demo interactions, tour starts and demo-to-contact conversion.

04
Put proof at the point of decision.
Rating, review count and licences sit beside the call to action, never only on an About page.
KPI: Call and booking conversion and lead-to-opportunity rate.

05
Make coverage the first question for physical-service businesses.
A location chip, ZIP check or service-area finder in or next to the hero, wired to real coverage data: the Punctual Pros ZIP-code model and CET's licensed states.
KPI: Out-of-area call rate down and qualified-lead share up.

06
Productize the service into a named offer.
Give the recurring program a name and a page of its own. Each portfolio OS page (ServiceOS, GridOS, FirmOS, LabOS, SignalOS, HarborOS) follows this pattern.
KPI: Recurring share of revenue, membership and contract attach, and exit multiple.

07
Make the company and acquisition story visible.
An Acquisitions or Partner with us link in the main navigation, founder stories and brand counts turn the website into a proprietary sourcing channel for add-ons.
KPI: Inbound seller conversations per quarter and share of add-ons sourced directly.

08
Give buyers self-serve tools for the jobs they repeat.
Calculators, price estimators, quick order, order history, documents and client portals, placed in the header or a utility bar rather than the footer.
KPI: Tool completions to leads, reorder rate and support tickets per account.

09
Neutral base, one accent; typography carries the brand.
An off-white or near-black canvas, one accent for actions and a mono face for numbers. Colour carries meaning, never decoration.
KPI: Perceived quality in user tests and call-to-action salience.

10
Offer an assistant grounded in your own data, placed where questions come up.
An Ask panel over the company's own data and FAQ, with example questions and labelled sources.
KPI: Questions answered without a person, assisted conversion and returns rate.

Source: design references, 26 reference homepages reviewed and captured on October 6, 2026.

FAQ
15 questions

Which states do you work in?
About ten states across New England and the Mid-Atlantic (reported), including Massachusetts, Connecticut, Rhode Island, New Hampshire, Maine and Vermont. Crews work out of Worcester, Taunton and Norwell, MA and Canton, CT.

Do you take projects in New York City or outside New England?
No. CET has no New York City plan. For sites outside our licensed states we are happy to refer you.

What does Horton Electrical Services do within CET?
Horton Electrical Services (Canton, CT; founded 1976) joined in September 2026 and leads municipal water: wastewater and pump-station electrical, SCADA, generators, solar O&M, civil site work and 24/7 emergency response.

What is NuWave Energy Solutions?
NuWave Energy Solutions (Norwell, MA) joined in October 2025: LED and controls retrofits, HVAC and process-load optimization, utility incentives (such as Mass Save) and measurement & verification.

Can you upgrade a wastewater plant or pump station electrical system?
Yes, Horton’s core work: MCCs, switchgear, VFDs, generators, transfer switches and SCADA, phased so the plant keeps treating, often on Clean Water SRF projects.

Do you offer 24/7 emergency generator and pump-station service?
Yes. The 24/7 emergency desk dispatches crews from Canton CT, Worcester and Taunton for generator, transfer-switch, switchgear and pump-station calls. CET Assure customers get priority dispatch.

How do you price work?
Design-build: fixed price after a site walk and preliminary design.
Bid-build: lump-sum bids on public and GC packages.
Service: time-and-materials or an annual CET Assure contract.
Efficiency: priced net of utility incentives, with savings verified.

Which incentive and funding programs can you help with?
SMART 3.0 and CT NRES (solar), Mass Save (efficiency), MassEVIP and NEVI (EV charging), resilience grants and state Clean Water SRF programs.

Do you install and operate EV chargers?
Yes. Level 2 and DC fast chargers for fleets, transit depots, campuses and municipalities, including on-street, with make-ready, utility coordination and network operation through GridOS.

Will you maintain a solar array you did not build?
Yes. O&M on existing PV and storage: inspection, inverter service, monitoring and truck rolls. Most owners move to a CET Assure contract.

What is CET Assure?
CET Assure is one annual contract for inspection, maintenance, monitoring and 24/7 response on pump stations, generators, switchgear, solar and EV chargers: one contact, one invoice, one uptime report.

What is GridOS?
GridOS is the operating layer behind CET: bid board, estimating, field coordination, fleet and pump-station monitoring, EV network operations and NuWave M&V. See GridOS →

Are you hiring electricians and apprentices?
Yes: journeyman electricians, apprentices, SCADA technicians, solar O&M technicians, estimators and energy engineers in Worcester, Taunton, Norwell and Canton CT. Training is paid; multi-state licensing is supported.

How quickly do you respond to a bid or quote request?
Within one business day. For public bids, put us on the plan-holder list so we can walk the site before bid day.

Is CET acquiring other contractors?
Yes. Six add-ons so far, four of them reported: NuWave (2025) and Horton (2026) are confirmed. Owners can start a confidential conversation.

Memo

Fix the base, then buy growth with doors, not debt.

Memo · 13 points
the 60-second read

This starts from a hypothesis for management to confirm. If our outside-in estimate is right (~$27M of revenue, range $20–35M, built from web traffic rather than company data), Fair Harbor is about 4.5 years in and at or below its 2021 entry scale (est. $30–40M), with low single-digit EBITDA and no add-ons.
The shift to a year-round lifestyle brand has already happened on the shelf: 64.0% of the 372 live products are non-swim, and golf, kids, collegiate and B2B custom launched in 2025–2026.
Margin is the problem: 38.5% of live variants are marked down, women's was cleared at ~70% off, and swim is the most-returned category at Shopify brands (21.6%).
So the first six months are about fixing the base (markdown discipline, fit and returns, and buying to forecast) before we pay for growth.
Chubbies is the proof case for the next step: at $122.9M it takes 51.9% of sales from wholesale and retail, that channel grew 16.3% last year, and its DTC fell 20.8% in Q2 2026.
Our plan is to take Fair Harbor from ~250 specialty doors to ~520 over 36 months through golf pro shops, campus bookstores and coastal specialty, using commissioned reps rather than new owned stores.
Retention is the cheapest growth: repeat-purchase benchmarks are 20–30%, and Klaviyo flows earn about 41% of email revenue from 5% of sends.
HarborOS, at an est. $0.3–0.7M, puts nine agents on that work (fit, CX, returns-to-exchange, demand planning, markdowns, lifecycle, paid media, cross-border and wholesale reorders); vendor claims include 60% ticket automation and 17% fewer fit returns.
International starts in month 30 as merchant-of-record DTC into Canada, the UK and Australia, following Vuori's e-commerce-first launch, because the store ships only to the US today.
We should stay capital-light: operating cash and an ABL of roughly $3.4–4.6M (est.) cover the plan, with a small sponsor follow-on as the backstop. Solo Brands' delisting shows what term debt does to a swim brand.
The roadmap assumes revenue grows from ~$27M to ~$40M and EBITDA from ~$1.6M to ~$5.2M by month 36. That is still below Chubbies' 18% margin, and every figure is an analyst assumption, not company data. On revenue, that only takes the business back to the top of the estimated entry range.
Measured from entry, the default exit case is weak: about 1.38x the est. entry EV midpoint over ~7.5 years, roughly 4.4% a year of EV growth. Measured from today's value at the same multiple, it earns about 21% a year. So the real decision is exit timing, which the Financing section sets out.
The Smith + Howard lesson applies: buyers paid for a scaled, legible portfolio company, so the exit story is wholesale breadth, repeat-customer economics and margin, and the logical buyers are strategics and brand owners.

Smith + Howard steps and analogs
what each move means here

Step 1 · Smith + Howard
Entry: founder-led regional leader, first institutional capital
BSP made a strategic anchor investment in Smith + Howard (Atlanta, ~100 professionals, one office) in Nov 2022.
Fair Harbor translation. Fair Harbor is the same set-up in consumer: a founder-led brand taking its first institutional capital ($30.7M Form D, Mar 2022). The S+H lesson is that the entry thesis named the adjacent services up front; Fair Harbor's equivalent is a named category-and-channel map (year-round apparel, golf, collegiate, B2B, international).

Step 2 · Smith + Howard
First adjacent-market step: merge with a like-minded firm next door
Merged with Market Street Partners (Chattanooga) in Aug 2023, its first move beyond Atlanta.
Fair Harbor translation. For Fair Harbor the 'next city' is the next door type: green-grass golf pro shops via FootJoy (18 collab SKUs) and sporting-goods doors like Scheels, before any new owned store.

Step 3 · Smith + Howard
Capability add-ons that widen the menu sold to existing clients
Added benefit-plan audit (JMM CPAs, Chicago, Jan 2024) and executive search (VIP Search/VIP Solutions, Dallas, Apr 2024).
Fair Harbor translation. Category extension is Fair Harbor's version: 372 live products, 64.0% of them non-swim, plus kids (51) and B2B custom (88 SKUs). Every new category should be sold first to the existing customer file and the existing door list.

Step 4 · Smith + Howard
Density in a chosen region, deal after deal
Fahrenheit Advisors (Richmond, Dec 2024), Smith Kesler (Carolinas, Jan 2025), Horton Lee & Burnett (Birmingham, Sep 2025), Bauknight Pietras & Stormer (SC, Jan 2026).
Fair Harbor translation. Fair Harbor should build door density in its proven coastal and golf geographies (Northeast, Florida, the Carolinas) before spreading thin, so reps, trunk shows and co-op marketing are shared across doors.

Step 5 · Smith + Howard
Technology, AI and offshore delivery as the margin engine
Per the exit release, BSP invested in leadership, technology, AI-enabled capabilities and an offshore delivery centre in India; Geels Norton (cyber, Feb 2026) added a tech-heavy service line.
Fair Harbor translation. HarborOS is the consumer equivalent: fit/size, CX, returns-to-exchange and demand-planning agents on Shopify/Klaviyo, sized at $0.3–0.7M for 2–5 points of EBITDA margin (ServiceOS evidence, est.).

Step 6 · Smith + Howard
The exit: a scaled, buyer-legible portfolio company sold to a growth investor
Sold to TPG (TPG Growth), closed Aug 6 2026 after ~3.5 years: ~100 to ~800 professionals, 1 to 11 Southeast locations plus India, 9 add-ons, nearly 4x revenue.
Fair Harbor translation. Fair Harbor is ~4.5 years into its hold with no add-ons. The S+H template says the exit story must be a scaled company with visible recurring earnings; for a brand that means wholesale breadth, repeat-customer economics and margin, not just top-line.

Vertical analog 1
Chubbies (Solo Brands)
Net sales FY2025: $122.9M

Wholesale retail share: 51.9%

Segment EBITDA margin: 18.2%

Acquisition price: $129.5M

This is the clearest proof that wholesale breadth, not DTC alone, carries a men's swim brand past $100M; and that a leveraged owner (Solo was delisted in July 2026 with ~$249M debt) can damage a good brand. It is also a possible add-on or door-share opportunity if Chubbies is sold.
Source: sec.gov
Confidence: high

Vertical analog 2
Vuori
International markets 2022: 7

Valuation 2021: $4B

US store plan: 100

International should start as localized DTC in English-speaking coastal markets with a merchant-of-record partner and a few premium wholesale partners, as Vuori did, not with owned stores.
Source: mr-mag.com
Confidence: medium

Vertical analog 3
Faherty Brand
Brand value or revenue: $250M

Stores: 80

Founded: 2013

The closest positioning analog to Fair Harbor (coastal, year-round lifestyle). It shows the ceiling of the category, but its store-heavy route is capital-intensive; Fair Harbor should borrow the specialty-door relationships and year-round assortment, not the 80-store fleet.

What each instrument means
implication per instrument

Sponsor equity at entry (Form D). History only: the $6.0M gap is an offering amount never filled in March 2022, not committed or undrawn capital today. HarborOS is funded from operating cash or the ABL, or a small sponsor follow-on.
Asset-based revolver history and likely refinancing. Same-day lien release and IP move to a Topco usually mean a new lender or a restructured collateral package. Diligence should confirm the current facility, covenants and whether store leases sit inside the borrowing base.
Sector norm: ABL advance rates. An ABL sized to Fair Harbor's working capital is roughly $3.4–4.6M (est.), enough to fund the seasonal swim build and wholesale receivables without term debt.

Cautionary precedent: leveraged owner of the closest rival. Debt, not the brand, is what broke the Chubbies owner. It also creates an opening: Chubbies or its doors could come loose, and Fair Harbor's light balance sheet makes it a credible buyer or partner.
Legacy government debt. Immaterial today; payoff status not public. Confirm it was repaid at the 2022 close.

Evidence by risk
public sources

Risk 1 · The baseline itself is an estimate. Fair Harbor has never disclosed revenue, EBITDA or debt; the $27M / 6% baseline is the midpoint of a $20–35M, 0–12% low-confidence range, and it sits at or below the est. 2021 entry scale.
Risk 2 · Markdown dependence erodes the brand. 38.5% of live variants were marked down in Sept 2026 and the women's line was cleared at ~70% off (live Shopify catalog, 24 Sep 2026; women's update page, Dec 2025).
Risk 3 · Weather and a single peak season. Swim is the most-returned category at Shopify brands (21.6%, an industry benchmark) and sales peak May–July; a cold, wet summer hits revenue and inventory together.
Risk 4 · DTC demand is softening across the category. Fair Harbor web visits fell 19.6% month on month (Similarweb, Aug 2026); Chubbies DTC fell 20.8% in Q2 2026.
Risk 5 · Wholesale credit exposure. Fair Harbor appears in the J.Crew (2020) and Express (2024) bankruptcy dockets (CourtListener); more doors means more receivables.
Risk 6 · Website accessibility litigation. Two ADA website suits in S.D.N.Y. (2024, settled; Jul 2026, open) (CourtListener).
Risk 7 · Unknown current lender and covenants. The eCapital ABL lien was released on Dec 11, 2025, the same day the core marks moved to a Topco; the new facility is not public (USPTO lien records).
Risk 8 · AI vendor claims are upper bounds. Every agent metric is vendor- or research-reported and self-selected.

Fit and size AI. Size and inseam on every product page and in chat, with a confidence score. Learns from what customers keep, not what they click.
Replenishment and retention. Post-purchase fit checks, pre-summer replenishment, cross-sell and win-back flows timed to the swim calendar.

Traceability ledger. A lot code on every care label links the trunk to its bottle, flake, pellet, yarn, fabric and factory documents.

Risks and mitigations

What could go wrong, and the guardrail for each.

Risk 01
Vendor claims are upper bounds
Pilot on swim product pages with a holdout group; scale only on measured lift; prefer outcome-based pricing.

Risk 02
Baselines are estimates
Replace with actuals in the first 30 days; every calculator input is already a slider.

Risk 03
Seasonality compresses learning
Fit and flows live before April; train on prior seasons' returns and orders.

Risk 04
Wholesale channel conflict
MAP rules, allocation by door tier, and wholesale-first drops for core prints.

Risk 05
Markdown habit
SKU-level markdowns only; content-led capture instead of blanket discounts.

Risk 06
Building too much software
Buy the systems of record; build only the data layer, fit tuning and ledger.

Evidence by risk
what each guard answers

Vendor claims are upper bounds. True Fit (up to 40%) and Bold Metrics (17%) report their own best cases.
Baselines are estimates. Revenue ($20–35M) and EBITDA (0–12%) are low-confidence outside-in estimates.
Seasonality compresses learning. Swim demand is concentrated in a few summer months, so a late launch loses a year.
Wholesale channel conflict. Portal reorders and DTC promotions can collide on price and allocation.
Markdown habit. 38.5% of live variants were marked down in Sept 2026; customers learn to wait.
Building too much software. Custom platforms become the next owner's write-off.

Why buyers pay
one line per proof point

Cohort curves, not anecdotes. Repeat and return rates by cohort, live in the data layer, are the first thing a DTC buyer asks for and the hardest to fake.
Inventory discipline on the record. Weeks of cover, sell-through and markdown share by SKU tell a working-capital story that supports the margin case.
A wholesale channel with reorder data. Door-level sell-through and pre-books show a scalable second channel; Chubbies' retail and wholesale reached 52% of FY2025 sales.
Sustainability claims that survive diligence. Lot-level traceability turns "made from bottles" from marketing into documentation, and protects the B Corp brand premium.

FAQ

Questions procurement will ask.

Do you support AM Law 200 firms?
Yes. Frontline serves 900+ law firms, including more than 50% of the AM Law 200 and 28% of the AM Law 50 (company release, June 2026). Law firms are the only clients Frontline serves.

What is included in the 24/7 service desk?
A legal-trained desk staffed 24/7/365 from nine hubs: VIP lines, DMS, time entry, onboarding and trial support. It runs on HELIX, Frontline's AI-optimized desk.

How do you handle eBilling, rejections and A/R?
Frontline checks LEDES invoices against outside counsel guidelines, submits them, works rejections and appeals, and follows up on A/R. FirmOS targets a rejection rate of 11%, down from 18% (est.).

What cybersecurity services do you provide?
Managed detection and response with a 24/7 SOC, email and phishing defense, vulnerability and patch management, privileged-access hygiene, incident response and tabletop drills, plus the evidence packs your clients' security questionnaires and OCGs require.

How is pricing structured?
Concept answer: managed IT and the service desk are scoped as a per-user monthly subscription, and eBilling and A/R are priced on volume. The assessment ends with a fixed proposal, so there are no surprises at renewal.

Which offices do you operate from?
Nine hubs: St. Louis (HQ), Toledo, Honolulu, New York, Toronto, London, Hyderabad, Goa and Cape Town. Together they provide follow-the-sun coverage, so the desk is staffed every hour of every day.

What are your support hours?
24 hours a day, 7 days a week, 365 days a year, including holidays and filing-deadline nights.

Do you offer co-managed IT for firms with an internal IT team?
Yes. Many larger firms keep IT leadership and strategy in-house while Frontline runs the desk, after-hours coverage, security operations or billing operations alongside them.

How long does onboarding take?
Three steps: Assess (weeks 1–3), Transition (typically days 30–90, with a runbook-driven cutover and parallel run on the desk), then Run & improve with monthly scorecards. (Concept timeline.)

How each step is computed

Enterprise value = EBITDA × multiple. Today: $8M × 6.8x = $54.4M. Month 36: $30M × (6.8x + 1.0 turn) = $234M, or 4.3x today's EV, gross of add-on capital. Capstone/IMAP put typical middle-market deals at 6.8x and premium deals at 9.8x. PKF puts project-heavy contractors at 5–6x and repeatable service at 10x+. Risks and mitigations
High
Every baseline is an estimate Run a 30-day data request; re-base roadmap and levers on actuals.

High

BLS expects ~81,000 electrician openings a year, and ABC says 499K net new construction workers are needed in 2026. Growth stalls if crews can’t be staffed.

Horton is third-generation and founder-led, and it holds the CT wastewater relationships. McKinsey finds ~70% of mergers miss their revenue-synergy targets.

Medium
Sponsors competing for the same targets Lead with founder rollover and a partner model, not banker auctions.

15 New England electrical/energy firms are already sponsor-owned. 16 PE firms overlap with CET, 5 rated high threat. Crete United’s RELCO is ~10 miles from Taunton.

Bonding capacity and public-bid exposure Arrange surety early; bid selectively; cap public hard-bid share.
Detail

Surety capacity, debt terms and DCAMM certification are not public. SRF project values are applicant estimates, not awards.
Mitigation: Arrange surety introductions early. Bid selectively through GridOS go/no-go scoring, and keep public hard-bid work below a set share of backlog.

Union and merit-shop mix Run union add-ons as divisions beside the IEC merit-shop lane.

CET shows as non-union on OSHA records, and several targets (e.g., McDonald’s ANJ division, Murphy, Averill) are union. That limits which crews can take which public or utility jobs.

Data-center hype Price it as an option inside the GridOS turn range.
Detail

ISO-NE says New England data-center load lags other regions, so data-center electrical is upside, not the core of the plan.
Mitigation: Price it as an option. GridOS value is booked only inside the 0.5–1.5-turn evidence range.

Ten-point thesis
Punctual Pros' three franchise brands all promise punctuality, so the ads should sell that promise (One Hour's 'Always On Time... Or You Don't Pay A Dime!', Ben Franklin's $5-a-minute guarantee, Mister Sparky's 'America's On-Time Electrician') rather than invent new claims.
Google Local Services Ads are the cheapest high-intent leads in the category ($39-57 per lead at a ~44% book rate, SearchLight Feb 2026), so LSA is the always-on base and is managed through reviews and fast answer rates rather than bids.
Self-serve CTV has dropped to $50-$500 minimums and roughly $15-40 CPMs with zip targeting (Vibe, Disney Campaign Manager, Universal Ads, YouTube on TV screens), which lets a ~$22M franchisee buy TV in its ~240 zips without paying for the whole Harrisburg or Philadelphia DMA.
CTV's job is to make the brand familiar before the furnace fails and to lift branded search and LSA conversion, so it is judged on cost per booked job and geo-holdout lift, not completion rate (which is ~94-99% by construction).
New-mover direct mail is the highest-intent prospect list a home-services company can get: county deed records show ~2,300 arm's-length residential sales a month in the PA core and ~1,150 on the Jersey Shore, each a household that must pick an HVAC, plumbing and electrical provider within months.
One in three of those PA buyers bought a pre-1980 home, which drives the Ben Franklin and Mister Sparky older-home inspection offers and the CTV zip weighting toward older housing stock (Punctual Pros ZIP coverage older-housing share).
The weather index ties it together: NWS alerts for Punctual Pros' zones (the demand model's weather-response plans) trigger budget multipliers and creative swaps 12-36 hours before demand spikes, so spend lands when calls are about to rise rather than after phones are already full.
The same deed feed becomes the CTV and Meta audience (address-matched households) and the mail list, so one new mover sees a coordinated welcome across mailbox, TV and phone, measured against a random holdout.
Test first with an 8-week, $50k/month Central PA pilot: LSA profile and review clean-up, a zip-level CTV geo holdout in the 61 Tier-I zips, and a mail-versus-holdout new-mover drip, all on unique call-tracking numbers in ServiceTitan.
If measured cost per booked job beats the modelled ~$185-200 blended, scale to the Jersey Shore (zip-only CTV) and then a regional Mid-Atlantic program, which also leaves a documented, attributed customer-acquisition engine for the exit data room.

Incrementality, margin, sources

Conservative case for Phase 1 (Central PA, Nov 2026 – Apr 2027): attributed jobs cut for incrementality (LSA, search and Meta 50%; CTV and mail 75%), contribution after technician labour, materials and ~7.5% franchise fees. At this level the plan adds ~12% to Punctual Pros’ ~$22M revenue and needs ~3 more technicians. Every figure is est. until the test reads it.

Local Services Ads base: $39–57 per lead at a ~44% book rate (SearchLight, Feb 2026); ranked by reviews and answer speed.

ZIP-targeted CTV: bought by ZIP, so spend stays near the Punctual Pros footprint.

New-mover mail: arm’s-length home buyers, a floor, from the county deed feeds already in the portal.

Weather triggers: a National Weather Service warning for a Punctual Pros county adds 50% to CTV for 72 hours and puts the storm cut live. It re-times spend: ~$5k a year at Phase 1 weights.

Method
how buyers a month are counted

Buyers / mo = arm’s-length residential sales (residential use, price > $1,000, not flagged non-arm’s-length) ÷ months in each county’s window, from Punctual Pros deed records (PA and NJ) as first pulled on Sep 24, 2026; the same definition as the plan. The records have been refreshed since, and this table keeps the Sep 24 figures so it matches the plan. PA: the 8 complete feeds count ~2,311/mo, which is the plan’s ~2,300. Dauphin’s feed stopped after 262 parcel pages, so it is left out; at its neighbours’ rate it would add ~340/mo (~2,651 in all). The plan’s 2,300 is therefore a floor, not an upward adjustment. Counting every priced transfer instead (incl. commercial and land) gives ~2,755/mo. NJ: whole-county count is ~1,237/mo over 9.5 dense months; the plan uses ~1,150 (about 7% lower), pending a zip-level split of Horvath’s service area. HU = housing units summed from the Punctual Pros ZIP-code model.

Trigger details
zone codes, test design, mail timing

Zone codes: Lancaster = PAC071 / PAZ066, Ocean = NJC029 / NJZ020; 11 counties mapped in the Punctual Pros demand model. Call multipliers are assumptions to calibrate on ServiceTitan.

Rules also fill the display tokens {alert} and {county}. The weather read is pre-registered before launch: the 9 PA counties are randomised for all of Phase 1, and every qualifying warning is a test event. Winter warnings are rare before January (22 of 28 PA winter warnings fell in Jan–Feb), so the read accumulates over the season.

County deed feeds: 9 PA counties plus Ocean and Monmouth NJ. CTV match uses address lists where the company supports it (Universal Ads custom lists, Vibe CRM upload). Response = any booking within 90 days, matched to ServiceTitan by address.

Hitting the 30-day window: PA parcel feeds lag the recorder by 1–5 weeks (Lancaster, York and Cumberland), so a weekly pull plus a 7-day print SLA puts card #1 in the mailbox within ~30 days of closing. NJ’s state SR1A file lags 3–4 months, so Horvath needs a county recorder or title-data feed.

Method
incremental, contribution, technicians

All outputs est. . Incremental = attributed jobs × incrementality (LSA, search, Meta 50%; CTV, mail, radio 75%), with mail split into the new-mover drip and lower-response saturation pieces. Contribution = revenue × (40% gross margin after technician labour and materials − 7.5% franchise royalty and brand fund) − media. Annual revenue % = 12 × monthly revenue ÷ ~$22M FY2025 pro forma revenue (Punctual Pros public filings, est.; range $16–28M); Phase 3 also covers add-on territories, so its base will be larger. Techs = jobs ÷ 45 per technician-month (assumption: ~2.2 jobs per technician-day × ~20.5 working days; replace with ServiceTitan). Phase 2 starts only if the Phase 1 read beats the conservative case. Phase 3 scales only channels whose measured incremental cost per job beats plan by ≥20%.

Unique call-tracking numbers per channel/creative and UTM + QR per spot (ServiceTitan call attribution)

Membership adds = booked jobs x 0.60 new-customer share (assumption) x 0.25 attach
Membership value a year ($) = membership adds x $20 x 12

Contribution = incremental revenue × (0.40 − 0.075) − media = +$23,618

Risks

Risks and mitigations.

High risk
Franchisor constraints
Authority Brands sets brand standards and may mandate parts of the tech stack; royalties (~7.2–7.5% of revenue) cap margin upside.
Mitigation: Pilot with franchisor sign-off; build only in the layers the FDD leaves to the franchisee (data, dispatch logic, outreach).

High risk
No Punctual Pros actuals yet
Every KPI baseline is an industry benchmark. Booking rate, members and ticket are not public.
Mitigation: Month 1–2 data spine sprint; replace every est. with ServiceTitan actuals before the investment committee.

Medium risk
AI on the phone
A bad 2 a.m. call costs a member. Vendor booking lifts are unaudited.
Mitigation: After-hours first, human hand-off on urgency words, weekly call scoring, opt-out to a person on request.

Medium risk
Cold outreach
Calling new movers cold is a poor first touch; mail first, then call the ones who respond.
Mitigation: Mail first; call only people who respond; do-not-contact lists synced daily.

Medium risk
Technician adoption
Tablets, pricebooks and coaching fail if techs see them as surveillance.
Mitigation: Tie spiffs to good-better-best adoption; lead techs pilot first; coaching is opt-in for month one.

Low risk
Model error in the Index
Most cold, plumbing and electrical multipliers are assumptions, not fitted elasticities.
Mitigation: Regress 12+ months of Punctual Pros booked calls on GHCN weather; publish error bands; staff to the band, not the point.

liner and shell

BreezeKnit liner. The scratchy mesh liner is the reason guys stop wearing swim trunks. BreezeKnit replaces it with a soft, stretchy knit that moves with you and dries fast, so the trunks go from the water to lunch without the chafe.
