FAQ

Questions, answered.

Ask the helper

How do the swim trunks fit?
Our trunks run true to waist size with an elastic back waistband and a drawcord. S fits a 28–30" waist, M 31–33", L 34–36", XL 37–39". Between sizes? Try the fit finder. Concept size chart.

What are the swim trunks made of?
The shell of our core trunks is spun from recycled plastic bottles, roughly 11 bottles per pair. Bottles are cleaned, melted and spun into quick-dry yarn. Each product page lists its fibres.

What is the BreezeKnit liner?
BreezeKnit is our anti-chafe liner: a soft, stretchy knit in place of the usual scratchy mesh. It lives in the Bayberry and Anchor trunks. Boardshorts skip the liner so you can wear your own base layer in surf.

What is the return and exchange policy?
Free exchanges on every US order, and returns within 30 days of delivery for unworn items with tags (swim liners must be intact). Exchanges ship when the carrier scans your box. Proposed policy.

How much is shipping and how long does it take?
Free standard shipping on US orders over $100; most orders ship in 1–2 business days and arrive in 3–5. Expedited options are shown at checkout. We currently ship within the United States only. Proposed policy for this concept.

Do you sell wholesale?
Yes. Fair Harbor is carried by department stores, 250+ specialty surf, resort and coastal shops, sporting-goods retailers, golf pro shops and campus stores. Store buyers can browse line sheets, pre-book and reorder in the wholesale portal (demo).

Do you do custom or corporate orders with logos and embroidery?
Yes. Our B2B custom program covers trunks, shirts, shorts and sweatshirts with custom embroidery for companies, clubs, weddings and events. Tell the helper your quantity and date, or email the team from the contact link in the footer.

Is Fair Harbor a B Corp?
Fair Harbor Clothing is a Public Benefit Corporation and a Certified B Corporation (B Impact score 94.3; 80 qualifies). The brand reports 27M+ plastic bottles recycled into its products.

Where are your stores?
Visit our own stores in SoHo, New York (Prince St) and Palm Beach Gardens, Florida, or find us at department stores, specialty shops, golf pro shops and campus stores.

What is Pre-Loved / Harbor Again trade-in?
Harbor Again (proposed) takes back worn Fair Harbor trunks for store credit. Good-condition pairs are cleaned and resold as Pre-Loved; the rest are recycled. It keeps the bottles in use one more summer.

Punctual Pros' current membership count, review count, online-booking share and technician headcount are not public. Baselines marked 'analyst assumption' or shown as — must be replaced with company data.
Market-size figures vary by publisher: Mordor's US HVAC services estimate is $17.93B (2025) in its latest vintage and $21.16B in an older one. GMI's $26.5B is residential equipment, not services. No residential-only plumbing or electrical services size was verified.
Richmond, VA is named in Phase 3, but Punctual Pros ZIP-code model covers only PA, NJ, MD, NY and WV. So Richmond and DE have no ZIP-level figures. Authority territory counts cover only the 66 PA/NJ/MD/DE locations parsed in Punctual Pros add-on targets, not the national system.
Expanding the franchise footprint needs Authority Brands' territory approval and transfer consent. Converting independents to franchise brands, or acquiring outside the franchise system, may face territorial restrictions not analysed here.
Generac's ~6.5% home-standby penetration and the Frontdoor 10-K figures were taken from summaries of the filings (SEC ARS PDF; StockTitan 10-K summary), not read line by line.

Terms

TEV: total enterprise value. FDD: franchise disclosure document. LSA: Google Local Services Ads. CSR: customer service rep. AP/AR: bills paid and bills collected. SOFR: the benchmark rate loans are priced over.

Design rationale

Lead with the number
Put the four numbers the deal team gets asked about in the first screen.

Entry to exit on a dated timeline

Show density on a map

Answers on demand

Closed Dec 14, 2021; maturity Dec 14, 2027. MFIC Jun-2026: term loan par $32.85M marked at 88.3% of par; revolver $2.35M drawn, $0.74M undrawn; total facility $180-300M est. .
Source: sec.gov

Coupon history: PIK amendment and return to cash pay
Cash interest coverage is ~1.0-1.3x est. . Working-capital release (DSO, inventory) is the fastest internal source of cash.
Terms and facts

Q4-2024 amendment converted part of the coupon to PIK (SOFR+340 cash + 4.50% PIK); principal accreted ~4.4% in 2025; Q1-2026 the loan returned to all-cash SOFR+640.
Source: sec.gov

Sponsor equity: BSP-TS, LP and preferred top-ups
New money is likely to come as preferred or structured equity. Add-ons in the next 12 months must be small, cash-light (earn-outs, seller notes, rollover equity) or funded with new capital.
Terms and facts

BSP-TS, LP raised $236.1M at close (Dec 2021), $257.1M cumulative by Jan 2024 (+$21.0M), with preferred units ranking above common.
Source: sec.gov

Sector leverage norms for a refinancing
At $25-35M est. EBITDA a market unitranche supports ~$130-220M of debt against $210-310M est. outstanding. Closing that gap needs EBITDA growth to ~$40-45M, equity paydown, or a lender-led…

Houlihan Lokey (Oct 2025) new-issue private credit for $20-100M EBITDA borrowers: unitranche 5.25x-6.25x at S+450-525, first lien 3.75x-4.75x; median net total leverage ~4.7x (Sep-2025).
Source: cdn.hl.com

Add-on valuation norms (tuck-in purchase multiples)
Small regional distributors bought at 5-7x and folded into a company valued higher add value through multiple arbitrage, but only once the company can fund them.
Terms and facts

Denville Scientific (2018) was bought for ~$20M on ~$25M revenue (~0.8x sales, ~35% gross margin). GF Data: average LMM purchase multiple 7.2x TTM adjusted EBITDA in 2025.

Method, sources and caveats

Method. Phase counts are computed from the portal's scored-site file (27,503 sites, aggregated by region only: counts by vertical, priority label and archetype, plus summed 2023 CMS allowed amounts) and its top-500 parent-organization file. Add-on targets come from the portal's 25-company Thomas screen (ZoomInfo revenue estimates). Capital structure and company estimates come from SEC filings research; lab-distribution medians from public comparables; Calibre and Sterling from the sponsor landscape; the Smith + Howard timeline and Thomas add-ons from the BSP firm profile; LabOS benchmarks from the portal's tech-premium evidence. External evidence was gathered on Oct 6, 2026 by web search and direct fetches of SEC filings (Avantor FY2025 10-K, VWR FY2014 10-K), state/federal pages (NJDOL), banker reports (Houlihan Lokey) and vendor case studies. Growth-lever and KPI targets are benchmarks or labelled assumptions; the KPI roadmap is an analyst assumption anchored to the Thomas Scientific filings estimate table.
Caveats.
Thomas Scientific's first-lien loan matures December 14, 2027 (88.3% of par in the lender's June 2026 10-Q); est. leverage 7-10x. Every lever is sequenced behind liquidity and refinancing.
Company revenue, EBITDA and headcount are low-confidence analyst estimates (Thomas Scientific filings), not company disclosures; the KPI roadmap inherits that uncertainty.
Thomas lab-site list scores are from a legacy targeting tool (NPPES, CMS 2023, CLIA, Hospital Compare); site counts are aggregated by region only, and the CMS allowed amount is Medicare billing, not lab-supply spend.
Vendor case studies (InstaLILY, Conexiom, Algolia, Conga/PROS, HighRadius, Flagship VMI) are self-reported and unaudited; treat them as upper bounds. weeks to deploy values are analyst estimates.
Market-size figures for cleanroom, cannabis testing and healthcare cold chain come from market-research firms whose forecasts vary widely.
The McKinsey forecasting figures and the Antylia/GTCR details come from search-engine extracts because the primary pages blocked automated fetches.
ZoomInfo revenue estimates for add-on targets are modeled and can be far off.

Risks
Risks and mitigations

Product data quality
High

Mitigation: Start with the top 5,000 SKUs by revenue; supplier data feeds; track search exit rate weekly.
Risk

Inconsistent units, packs and CAS fields break AI search matching.

Channel conflict with reps
High

Mitigation: Digital orders credit the account owner; pay reps on share of wallet and health.
Risk

Reps resist digital orders that bypass them.

Customer-side punchout lead times
Medium

Mitigation: Start with accounts already on Coupa/Jaggaer; offer a hosted catalog meanwhile.
Risk

Procurement teams control their own integration queue.

Capital constraints
Medium

Mitigation: Vendor-first, phased spend ($2–4M est. ); payback before the next phase.
Risk

Leverage limits discretionary spend; no big-bang replatform.

ERP and pricing complexity
Medium

Mitigation: One price service fed from the ERP; migrate acquired businesses in waves.
Risk

Contract price files span thousands of accounts and acquired businesses.
